questions.question: What is the central paradox exposed in the opening verse of Surah Al-Munafiqun?
options: A. The hypocrites denied the Prophet's messengership while secretly believing in it
B. The hypocrites made a technically true declaration about the Prophet yet Allah called them liars
C. The hypocrites refused to pray in public but worshipped in private
D. The hypocrites accepted Islam only after the Battle of Badr
questions.explanation: The hypocrites declared 'We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah,' which is factually correct, yet Allah immediately called them liars. As the tafsir explains, the lie lay in the contradiction between their spoken testimony and their hearts, which held no genuine inner belief.

questions.question: True or false: the hypocrites in verse 2 used false oaths as a spontaneous emotional response rather than a deliberate, calculated strategy.
questions.explanation: The Layer 1 tafsir explains that the Arabic 'ittakhadhu' means they adopted oath-swearing as a deliberate, calculated strategy. Whenever they sensed suspicion, they would preemptively swear loyalty to deflect accountability, turning sacred declarations into tools of systematic deception.

questions.question: Which young companion reported Abdullah ibn Ubayy's treacherous statements to the Prophet, and whose account was confirmed by the revelation of this surah?
options: A. Abdullah ibn Masud
B. Anas ibn Malik
C. Zaid ibn Arqam
D. Abu Hurayra
questions.explanation: Imam al-Tabari in his Jami al-Bayan records through multiple chains that Zaid ibn Arqam overheard Abdullah ibn Ubayy declare that 'the more honorable shall expel the more humble from Medina.' When Zaid reported this to the Prophet, the revelation of Surah Al-Munafiqun confirmed the truth of Zaid's account completely.

questions.question: True or false: Ibn Kathir described Abdullah ibn Ubayy and the leading hypocrites as physically unimpressive men whose danger lay purely in secret scheming.
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir in Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim, drawing on reports from Ibn Abbas, describes Abdullah ibn Ubayy as a man of striking physique, powerful presence, and considerable oratorical gifts. Verse 4 itself acknowledges their impressive bodies and compelling speech, making the Quranic comparison to hollow propped-up timber all the more striking.

questions.question: What arrogant boast did Abdullah ibn Ubayy make that verse 8 quotes directly, and what was the immediate divine counter-declaration?
options: A. He claimed Muslims would soon abandon the Prophet; Allah declared that faith cannot be extinguished
B. He claimed the more honored would expel the more humble from Medina; Allah declared that all honor belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers
C. He claimed he would take over leadership of Medina; Allah declared that leadership belongs to the righteous alone
D. He claimed the emigrants would starve; Allah declared that provision belongs to Him alone
questions.explanation: Verse 8 quotes ibn Ubayy's statement that 'the more honored will surely expel the more humble from Medina,' by which he meant the Prophet. Allah's immediate response overturns this entirely: 'To Allah belongs all honor, and to His Messenger, and to the believers.' As the tafsir notes, the man who boasted of his own honor was judged by the very Source of all honor.

questions.question: Verse 9 warns believers that wealth and children can distract them from something specific. What is that thing, and what label does Allah give those who allow this distraction to win?
options: A. From performing the hajj; they are called negligent
B. From the remembrance of Allah; they are called the losers
C. From giving zakat; they are called the wrongdoers
D. From seeking knowledge; they are called the heedless
questions.explanation: The verse warns that wealth and children must not distract believers from 'dhikr Allah,' the remembrance and awareness of Allah. It closes with the verdict: 'whoever does that, those are the losers.' The word 'khasirun' evokes someone who trades something precious for something worthless, as the tafsir explains.

questions.question: True or false: the dying person in verse 10 requests years of additional life in order to perform the hajj and complete major ritual obligations.
questions.explanation: The tafsir emphasizes that the dying person requests only an 'ajal qareeb,' a brief or near term. The regret is specifically about not giving charity and not being among the righteous. The deliberate modesty of the request makes the scene more painful, implying that even a little more time would have been enough if only it had been granted.

questions.question: What specific economic strategy did Abdullah ibn Ubayy urge against the Prophet's community, and which group was most directly targeted?
options: A. He urged Medinan traders to raise prices on Muslims; wealthy companions were the target
B. He urged sympathizers among the Ansar to cut off material support from the Meccan emigrants until they abandoned the Prophet
C. He organized a tax boycott to deprive the Prophet's state of revenue
D. He called for blocking the roads to Medina to prevent Muslim pilgrims from entering
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir in Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim, relying on Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, explains that ibn Ubayy urged his sympathizers among the Ansar to cut off support from the Muhajirun. Imam al-Tabari records through narrations from Ibn Abbas and Zaid ibn Arqam that this strategy was particularly cruel since the emigrants had sacrificed everything for their faith and depended entirely on Medinan hospitality.

questions.question: Wahbah al-Zuhayli highlights the divine name used to close Surah Al-Munafiqun. Which name is it, and why does he consider it the surah's ultimate answer to hypocrisy?
options: A. Al-Aziz, because it establishes Allah's absolute power over the hypocrites' schemes
B. Al-Ghafur, because it holds open the door of forgiveness even for the worst sinners
C. Khabir, because it signifies penetrating knowledge of inner realities, meaning Allah was never deceived by the hypocrites' outward performance
D. Al-Qadir, because it affirms that Allah could have destroyed the hypocrites at any moment
questions.explanation: Wahbah al-Zuhayli in Al-Tafsir al-Munir draws particular attention to the closing divine name 'Khabir,' one who has deep and penetrating knowledge of inner realities. He argues it is carefully chosen as the surah's final word: whatever success the hypocrites achieved in deceiving humans was entirely irrelevant before Allah the Khabir, who saw through every false performance from the very beginning.
